Hi Mina / Arjun,

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the quick facts and Currentsys' GSTIN. Short answer: we should NOT withhold GST on the credit if the credit is simply an adjustment reducing the value of prior taxable supply that was already zero-rated/treated as B2B under reverse-charge. However, two checks are required before we confirm reverse-charge: 

1) Place of supply determination: since the services were consumed from EU-hosted infra, we need to confirm place-of-supply rules and whether Redwood treated the original invoices as B2B supply (VAT not charged). If original invoices were zero-rated or billed without VAT because the buyer accounted under reverse-charge, then the credit should mirror that treatment.

2) Evidence: we need a current GST registration snapshot and a statement from Currentsys confirming they are registered and will self-account (for audit trail). That snapshot can be the attached GST certificate but we also need the AP person name and a short signed confirmation (can be a one-line email).

If both checks pass: we reissue the credit as a non-VAT line item (mirror original invoice treatment) and no withholding. If they fail, we may need to reissue with a VAT line and Redwood remit (which will be odd for a credit).

Action items: 
- Arjun: please confirm with AP that Currentsys will self-account and reply to this thread (one-line is fine). Also please share the credit memo PDF (Inv-20260531-CR) — it helps us verify invoice linkage.
- Mina / Vanessa: once Arjun confirms, we update billing and reissue docs. Vanessa, FYI: may require credit memo reissue in our billing system and short note in the customer ledger.

Ben
Lead, Tax & Billing Ops
Redwood Inference
